position.summary: Houthi missiles struck the Riyadh airport, killing an Egyptian flight attendant, and Egypt pledged to offer any kind of support to Saudi Arabia. Approximately 72 artisanal gold miners died in an airstrike near the disputed Egypt-Sudan border, and both foreign ministries were expected to consult on whose aircraft fired. Baha'i families in Egypt faced a critical shortage of burial space, and the press union chief publicly rejected pressure over detained journalists while torture allegations surfaced in the Matsadaash case. The government prepared a 30 percent state-stake sale of Banque du Caire through the Egyptian stock exchange as a privatization signal, while inflation had slowed despite global price pressures. Restored Fayoum mummy portraits were unveiled and set to travel abroad for the first time. A US judge ordered the Trump administration to facilitate the return of an Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea. The US-brokered Gaza ceasefire had stalled a year after signing, and Egypt upgraded its strategic partnership with South Korea. The Zamalek-Al Ahly derby fed social-media debate, and FAA warnings over Saudi airspace opened a small transit opportunity for Cairo.

naive_forecast.summary: The naive reading takes the text's top-listed expectations at face value and ignores its own hedges and alternative scenarios. Egypt issues a formal foreign-ministry statement backing Saudi Arabia and pledging Red Sea shipping support within days of the Riyadh strikes. Egyptian and Sudanese foreign ministers hold a phone consultation over the gold mine airstrike. The Egyptian stock exchange opens the Banque du Caire IPO subscription period to retail investors as a privatization milestone. Baha'i families stage a small sit-in near the cemetery demanding additional burial plots. The foreign ministry announces the return of the Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea. The overall picture is managed instability: Cairo projects diplomatic strength, delivers a positive economic signal, and handles small domestic irritations without letting any one escalate into a full crisis.
